mechanics.mechanic: Open by naming the subject, connecting it to familiar assumptions, and previewing the practical problems the explanation will address. Frame the discussion as both conceptual and usable.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use at the beginning of an educational piece when the audience may recognize the topic but not understand its deeper significance.
mechanics.avoid: Do not promise outcomes that the explanation cannot support or overload the opening with an exhaustive list of benefits.

mechanics.mechanic: Distinguish the central question from adjacent topics, briefly acknowledge related areas, and state which ones will receive limited or no attention.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when the subject has multiple branches and readers need to know what the piece will and will not explain.
mechanics.avoid: Avoid introducing so many excluded topics that the scope statement becomes a second outline.

mechanics.function: Building from basic concepts to mechanisms
mechanics.mechanic: Begin with a plain-language definition, establish the relevant system or components, then progressively connect those components to the target behavior or outcome.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use for technical subjects where readers need a mental model before they can evaluate applications.
mechanics.avoid: Avoid introducing specialized terminology before explaining its function or relevance.

mechanics.mechanic: Translate an abstract process into a concrete, familiar model, then map each part of the analogy back to the underlying mechanism. Revisit the analogy as new layers are added.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when a process involves invisible, dynamic, or multistep changes that are difficult to visualize directly.
mechanics.avoid: Do not let the analogy replace the explanation, and explicitly mark where the comparison stops being exact.

mechanics.mechanic: Explain a process as a sequence of states—starting condition, trigger, rise or change, consequence, recovery, and possible repetition—rather than as a static relationship.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use for behavior, learning, adaptation, motivation, feedback, or any system in which timing affects the result.
mechanics.avoid: Avoid implying that every instance follows an identical sequence or that a simplified timeline captures every variable.

mechanics.mechanic: After describing an internal process, translate it into the subjective experience or observable behavior a person might notice. Then connect that experience back to the mechanism.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when the audience needs to understand how technical material relates to everyday decisions, habits, or symptoms.
mechanics.avoid: Do not treat a subjective experience as definitive proof of a particular biological process.

mechanics.mechanic: Introduce a typical pattern, then test it against contrasting outcomes such as stronger, weaker, delayed, or reversed responses. Use the contrasts to clarify which variables change the result.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when a simplified rule could otherwise be mistaken for a universal law.
mechanics.avoid: Avoid presenting unusual cases as representative or using exceptions without explaining what they reveal about the general model.

mechanics.mechanic: Distinguish the signal that drives current behavior from the information-processing system that updates future behavior. Explain how both operate in parallel and interact over time.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when an explanation involves both short-term motivation and longer-term adaptation.
mechanics.avoid: Avoid collapsing all effects into a single process or suggesting that learning automatically produces consistent behavior.

mechanics.mechanic: Pause after a dense section to restate the model in simpler terms, identify the few elements readers must retain, and then move to the next level of detail.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use in long technical explanations or whenever terminology and causal steps accumulate quickly.
mechanics.avoid: Do not repeat every preceding detail; compress the model around its functional relationships.

mechanics.function: Using an extreme case as a diagnostic
mechanics.mechanic: Examine an unusually strong or clear example first, use it to expose the governing variables, and then return to ordinary cases with a more nuanced interpretation.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when the core mechanism is easier to see at an extreme and can be transferred back to everyday situations.
mechanics.avoid: State clearly that the extreme case is illustrative, not automatically representative of normal conditions.
